items.summary: Despite progress in the political process in Libya, institutional divisions, economic deterioration and security fragility continue to threaten stability, the UN envoy warned the Security Council on Wednesday, calling on Libyan leaders to overcome their differences to pave the way for national elections.

items.title: Could your brain data be used against you? UN calls for limits on neurotechnology

items.title: The world is waging a ‘war on nature’ as progress on biodiversity targets lags

items.title: AI, green energy and economic transitions risk leaving vulnerable communities behind, UN warns

items.title: Afghanistan faces record hunger levels amid rampant rights violations
items.summary: Acute malnutrition and hunger in Afghanistan have reached the highest levels ever recorded, with 15.9 million people facing acute food insecurity and conditions set to worsen in the coming months, according to a global hunger monitor report released on Thursday.

items.title: Haiti sanctions renewed: Starving the gangs of bullets
items.summary: Haiti is living through one of the world’s most acute security crises. Armed gangs control large parts of the capital, Port-au-Prince, and are pushing into rural areas, terrorising communities, killing people, committing rape and other sexual assaults, kidnapping for ransom and extorting individuals and businesses.

items.title: DR Congo: Cholera cases spike amid fight against Ebola
